requirements.title: Changes and stacks
requirements.rationale: The change is the unit of work of the product (criteria 1 and 2 of section 16): if a push does not become a numbered, versioned, stackable change, nothing built on changes can be trusted.

criteria.condition: a git client pushes a new branch of a workspace with the push option parley.change and then pushes that branch four more times, one of them a forced push of rewritten history
criteria.action: open one change for the branch at the first push and record one new version of that same change at each later push
criteria.contract: GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo/changes/<number> answers 200 with the same number after every push; GET …/changes/<number>/versions lists versions 1 to 5, each with kind push and a distinct head_sha equal to the commit that push sent

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
a clone of demo made with stock git and alice's PAT
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/changes_test.go, TestChange_FivePushesGiveFiveVersions: out = git push -o parley.change origin feat; n = change number read from GET …/changes?state=open (one item, source branch feat); heads = [head]; repeat 3 times {commit; git push origin feat; heads += head}; git commit --amend; git push --force origin feat; heads += head; for each push assert get(…/changes/n).status == 200 and .number == n; v = get(…/changes/n/versions).items; assert [x.version for x in v] == [1,2,3,4,5]; assert [x.head_sha for x in v] == heads; assert all x.kind == 'push'; assert count(get(…/changes).items) == 1

criteria.action: for any version of a change, serve that version's head to a git fetch of refs/parley/changes/<number>/<version>, also after a forced push replaced it on the source branch
criteria.contract: git fetch origin refs/parley/changes/<number>/<v> exits 0 for v = 1 to 5 and FETCH_HEAD equals the head_sha of version v

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
a change with five versions made by five pushes, the last one forced
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/changes_test.go, TestChange_EveryVersionHeadIsFetchable: in a fresh clone, for v in 1..5: code = git fetch origin refs/parley/changes/<n>/<v>; assert code == 0; assert git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD == versions[v].head_sha; assert git cat-file -t FETCH_HEAD == 'commit'

criteria.condition: a push moves a change's source branch to the previous version's commits rebased, with no other edit, onto a newer head of the target branch
criteria.action: record the new version as patch-equivalent to its predecessor and report an empty interdiff between the two
criteria.contract: the new version has patch_equivalent_to equal to the previous version number; GET …/changes/<number>/diff?version=<new>&against=<previous> answers 200 with no changed file

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
an open change at version 1; main has since moved by a landed change that touches another file
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/changes_test.go, TestChange_PureRebaseHasEmptyInterdiff: git fetch; git rebase origin/main; git push --force origin feat; v2 = get(…/changes/n/versions/latest); assert v2.version == 2 and v2.patch_equivalent_to == 1; d = get(…/changes/n/diff?version=2&against=1); assert d.status == 200 and d.files == []; then amend a file's content, force push; v3 = latest; assert v3.patch_equivalent_to == null; assert get(…/diff?version=3&against=2).files names that file

criteria.condition: a client asks for the change of a commit that a land put on a protected branch
criteria.action: answer with the change, the version that was landed and the session named on the work
criteria.contract: GET …/changes/by-commit/<sha> answers 200 with the landed change's number; GET …/scm/commits/<sha> answers 200 with a change member naming that number and the landed version, and session_id equal to the session given on the push

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
a session S opened with parley session start demo; a change pushed with -o parley.session=S and landed
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/changes_test.go, TestChange_LandedCommitResolvesToChangeVersionAndSession: sha = landed_sha of the change's land attempt (get(…/changes/n/lands).items[0]), which is the head of main after the land; c = get(…/changes/by-commit/sha); assert c.status == 200 and c.number == n; k = get(…/scm/commits/sha); assert k.change.number == n and k.change.version == 1; assert k.session_id == S; assert cli(alice, 'change','find','demo',sha).json.number == n

criteria.condition: the workspace owner fast-forwards the protected default branch by a git push with an API key, and a client then asks for the pushed commit
criteria.action: report that the commit belongs to no change and record the push as a direct push
criteria.contract: GET …/scm/commits/<sha> answers 200 with change null; GET /api/v1/events/log?workspace=demo&types=parley.git.push holds one event whose metadata has ref refs/heads/main, after equal to the sha and direct true; GET …/changes lists no change for it

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/changes_test.go, TestChange_DirectOwnerPushResolvesToNoChange: in a clone with alice's API key: commit on main; code = git push origin main; assert code == 0; sha = HEAD; assert get(…/scm/commits/sha).change == null; ev = get(/events/log?workspace=demo&types=parley.git.push).items; e = the one with metadata.after == sha; assert e.metadata.ref == 'refs/heads/main' and e.metadata.direct == true; assert get(…/changes?state=open).items == []

criteria.condition: the bottom change of a stack of three, opened by pushing three branches each built on the one before, gets a new version
criteria.action: rebase each change above it onto the new head below it and record a version of kind restack on each, without any request from a client
criteria.contract: within 30 seconds of the push, changes 2 and 3 of the stack each have a latest version with kind restack and created_by.actor_type system; the new head of each has the new head of the change below it as an ancestor; depends_on of each is unchanged

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
branches a, b (on a) and c (on b) pushed in one git push with -o parley.change, giving changes A, B, C with B.depends_on == A and C.depends_on == B
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/stacks_test.go, TestStack_NewVersionBelowRestacksDependants: assert get(…/changes/A/stack).changes numbers == [A,B,C]; amend a's commit (edit a file only a touches); git push --force origin a; poll up to 30 s until get(…/changes/C/versions/latest).kind == 'restack'; vb = latest of B; vc = latest of C; assert vb.kind == 'restack' and vb.created_by.actor_type == 'system'; git fetch; assert git merge-base --is-ancestor <A.head_sha> <vb.head_sha> and --is-ancestor <vb.head_sha> <vc.head_sha>; assert B.depends_on == A and C.depends_on == B; the test sent no request between the push and the polls other than reads

criteria.condition: the bottom change of a stack lands
criteria.action: rebase the next change of the stack onto the target branch and clear its depends_on
criteria.contract: within 30 seconds of the land, the next change has depends_on null, a latest version of kind restack whose base_sha is the target's head, and needs_restack false; the change above it still depends on it

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
a stack of three changes A, B, C as above, all ready
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/stacks_test.go, TestStack_LandingBottomRebasesNextOntoTarget: r = post(…/changes/A/land); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.status == 'landed'; main = get(…/scm/refs/heads/main).sha; poll up to 30 s until get(…/changes/B).depends_on == null; b = get(…/changes/B); assert b.needs_restack == false; v = get(…/changes/B/versions/latest); assert v.kind == 'restack' and v.base_sha == main; assert get(…/changes/C).depends_on == B

criteria.condition: the restack of a dependent change onto a new version of the change below it conflicts
criteria.action: leave the dependant's source branch and versions as they were and mark the dependant as needing a restack, with a conflict report
criteria.contract: the dependant has needs_restack true, restack_reason conflict and mergeable conflict; GET …/changes/<number>/conflict answers 200 with a conflict report whose files name the conflicted path; the dependant's source branch head and its latest version number equal their values before the push below

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
changes A and B with B.depends_on == A, where B edits line 1 of shared.txt that A created
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/stacks_test.go, TestStack_ConflictingRestackMovesNothing: before = (get(…/scm/refs/heads/b).sha, get(…/changes/B).version); amend a so line 1 of shared.txt differs; git push --force origin a; poll up to 30 s until get(…/changes/B).needs_restack; b = get(…/changes/B); assert b.restack_reason == 'conflict' and b.mergeable == 'conflict'; rep = get(…/changes/B/conflict); assert rep.mergeable == 'conflict' and 'shared.txt' in [f.path for f in rep.conflict.files]; assert (get(…/scm/refs/heads/b).sha, b.version) == before

requirements.title: Task forks
requirements.rationale: An agent's first act is to fork (criterion 3): the fork must exist at once whatever the repository's size, must confine its token, and must go away by itself.

criteria.condition: an agent sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/<parent>/forks with a token object
criteria.action: answer in that one call with the fork, its git remote and a token value, with the fork usable by stock git as soon as the answer arrives
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with workspace.kind fork and workspace.status ready, a remote URL and token.token; a git clone of remote with that token, made with no wait after the answer, exits 0 and its HEAD equals the parent's default branch head; a push of a new branch with that token exits 0

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
alice's unbound PAT with workspaces:write and tokens:manage
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/forks_test.go, TestFork_OneCallGivesForkRemoteAndToken: r = post(…/workspaces/demo/forks, {token:{permissions:['git:read','git:write','changes:read','changes:write']}}); assert r.status == 201; assert r.workspace.kind == 'fork' and r.workspace.status == 'ready'; assert r.remote != '' and r.token.token starts with 'parley_pat_'; assert r.token.workspace == r.workspace.slug; code = git clone <remote with token>; assert code == 0 and HEAD == get(…/demo/scm/refs/heads/main).sha; commit on new branch t; assert git push origin t == 0; assert cli(pat,'fork','list','demo').json.items has the slug

criteria.condition: the suite runs with PARLEY_ACCEPTANCE_LARGE_REPO=1 and the parent's repository holds at least 1 GiB of history
criteria.action: create a fork that is usable at once, in a time that does not grow with the size of the parent's repository
criteria.contract: for a parent of at least 1 GiB and for a parent of 1 MiB, each of 20 fork creations is answered 201 in under 1 second, and the median for the large parent is at most 200 ms above the median for the small one; a git ls-remote of the large parent's fork with its token exits 0 immediately after the answer

setup: a hub started by the harness; alice; workspace small from a 1 MiB origin and workspace big from an origin the harness fills with incompressible blobs until its pack is at least 1 GiB, both ready
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/forks_test.go, TestLargeRepo_ForkCreationDoesNotGrowWithSize: harness.Require(t, LargeRepo); for ws in {small, big}: times[ws] = 20 x duration of post(…/workspaces/ws/forks, {token:{…}}) asserting 201 each; assert max(times[ws]) < 1 s; assert median(times.big) - median(times.small) <= 200 ms; r = last big fork; assert git ls-remote <r.remote with token> == 0 and lists refs/heads/main

criteria.condition: a request made with a fork's token names another workspace, or a route of the fork's parent other than the fork's own changes and the awareness and policy reads
criteria.action: refuse the request without revealing whether the other workspace exists
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with error_type not_found for a workspace outside the fork, the same answer as for a slug that does not exist; HTTP 403 with error_type token_bound for another route of the parent; a git fetch of the parent with the token fails with the repository not found; nothing is written

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
a second workspace other owned by alice; a fork F of demo created with a token that holds git, changes, scm, workspaces and audit scopes
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/forks_test.go, TestFork_TokenIsRefusedOutsideTheFork: a table over requests with F's token: {GET …/workspaces/other -> 404 not_found, GET …/workspaces/no-such -> 404 not_found, GET …/workspaces/other/scm/refs -> 404, GET …/workspaces/demo/scm/refs -> 403 token_bound, POST …/workspaces/demo/scm/commits -> 403 token_bound, PUT …/workspaces/demo/policy -> 403 token_bound, POST …/workspaces/demo/forks -> 403 token_bound}: assert status and error.error_type; assert body(other) == body(no-such) apart from the request id; assert git ls-remote <demo remote with F's token> != 0 and git ls-remote <other remote> != 0; assert demo's refs and policy revision are unchanged

criteria.condition: a request made with a fork's token reads or lands a change of the parent whose source is that fork, or reads the parent's activity or policy
criteria.action: serve the request as it would for the token's user
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 for GET of the fork's own change on the parent, for GET …/<parent>/activity?paths=… and for GET …/<parent>/policy; HTTP 404 for a change of the parent whose source is another fork

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
forks F and G of demo, each with a token and one open change on demo (numbers f and g)
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/forks_test.go, TestFork_TokenReachesOwnChangeAndParentReads: with F's token: assert get(…/workspaces/demo/changes/f).status == 200; assert get(…/workspaces/demo/activity?paths=**).status == 200; assert get(…/workspaces/demo/policy).status == 200; assert get(…/workspaces/demo/changes/g).status == 404; assert post(…/workspaces/demo/changes/f/land).status == 200

criteria.condition: a git client pushes to a tracking branch of a fork
criteria.action: refuse the push and leave the branch at the parent's head
criteria.contract: git push exits non-zero and its stderr holds 'tracks the parent workspace and is read-only in this fork'; git ls-remote of the fork still shows the branch at the parent's head

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
a fork F of demo with a token; a clone of F
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/forks_test.go, TestFork_PushToTrackingBranchIsRefused: commit on main in the clone; code, err = git push origin main; assert code != 0; assert 'tracks the parent workspace and is read-only in this fork' in err; assert git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main == get(…/workspaces/demo/scm/refs/heads/main).sha

criteria.condition: a fork is created with no ttl
criteria.action: set the fork to expire 7 days after its creation
criteria.contract: the fork's expires_at is exactly created_at plus 168 hours

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/forks_test.go, TestFork_DefaultLifetimeIsSevenDays: r = post(…/workspaces/demo/forks, {}); w = r.workspace; assert parse(w.expires_at) - parse(w.created_at) == 168 h; assert cli(alice,'workspace','get',w.slug).json.expires_at == w.expires_at

criteria.condition: the suite runs with PARLEY_ACCEPTANCE_LONG=1 and a fork's expires_at has passed
criteria.action: remove the fork and revoke its token
criteria.contract: within 7 minutes of creating a fork with ttl 5m: GET of the fork with its owner's API key answers 404 not_found; a request with the fork's token answers 401 unauthenticated; the event log holds parley.fork.expire for the fork with metadata.reason ttl; the fork answers 200 until 4 minutes after its creation

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/forks_test.go, TestLong_ForkDisappearsAtItsTTL: harness.Require(t, Long); r = post(…/workspaces/demo/forks, {ttl:'5m', token:{…}}); at +4 min assert get(…/workspaces/<fork>).status == 200; poll every 10 s until +7 min for get(…/workspaces/<fork>).status == 404; assert reached; assert get(/user, bearer fork token).status == 401; e = get(/events/log?workspace=demo&types=parley.fork.expire).items; assert one e with resource for the fork and metadata.reason == 'ttl'; assert the fork is absent from get(…/workspaces/demo/forks).items

requirements.title: Source control API and git compatibility
requirements.rationale: An agent without a checkout and a developer with stock git must reach the same repository and get the same result (criteria 4 and 14).

criteria.condition: a client with no clone reads a file, a tree, the history of a path, a diff between two commits and the blame of a file through the source control API
criteria.action: answer each read with the content of the repository
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 for each; the file bytes, the tree entries, the commit ids of the path's history, the changed paths of the diff and the commit id of each blamed line equal what stock git reports for a clone of the same workspace

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
the origin was seeded with three commits that touch src/a.txt and docs/b.md; a reference clone made with stock git
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/scm_test.go, TestSCM_ReadsMatchTheRepository: assert get(…/scm/file?path=src/a.txt&ref=main, raw).body == bytes of src/a.txt in the clone; assert names(get(…/scm/tree?ref=main&path=src).items) == git ls-tree --name-only main src/; assert [c.sha for c in get(…/scm/commits?path=src/a.txt).items] == git log --format=%H -- src/a.txt; assert paths(get(…/scm/diff?base=<c1>&head=<c3>).files) == git diff --name-only c1 c3; for each line of get(…/scm/blame?path=src/a.txt).lines assert its sha == git blame -l; the same five reads through parley scm cat|ls|log|diff|blame exit 0 with the same data

criteria.condition: a client sends POST …/scm/commits with operations that create, update and delete several files on a branch that does not exist, naming a base_ref
criteria.action: create one commit holding all the operations and create the branch at it
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with the new commit's sha; GET …/scm/refs/heads/<branch> answers that sha; the commit has one parent, the head of base_ref, and its diff against the parent lists exactly the operated paths

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/scm_test.go, TestSCM_CommitOfSeveralFiles: r = post(…/scm/commits, {branch:'api-work', base_ref:'main', message:'m', operations:[create x/1.txt, create x/2.txt, update src/a.txt, delete docs/b.md]}); assert r.status == 201; assert get(…/scm/refs/heads/api-work).sha == r.sha; k = get(…/scm/commits/r.sha); assert k.parents == [main head]; assert sorted(paths(get(…/scm/diff?base=main&head=api-work).files)) == ['docs/b.md','src/a.txt','x/1.txt','x/2.txt']

criteria.condition: a commit creation names an expected_head_sha that is no longer the branch's head
criteria.action: refuse the commit and report the branch's current head
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type ref_moved and error.details.current_sha equal to the branch's head; the branch has not moved and no commit was added

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
branch api-work created through the API at commit c1, then moved to c2 by a second API commit
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/scm_test.go, TestSCM_StaleExpectedHeadIsRefMoved: r = post(…/scm/commits, {branch:'api-work', expected_head_sha:c1, message:'late', operations:[create y.txt]}); assert r.status == 409 and r.error.error_type == 'ref_moved' and r.error.details.current_sha == c2; assert get(…/scm/refs/heads/api-work).sha == c2; code = cli(alice,'scm','commit','demo', … '--expected-head', c1).code; assert code == 1 and stderr error_type == 'ref_moved'

criteria.condition: a client with no clone creates a commit on a new branch, opens a change for it and lands the change, all through the REST API
criteria.action: land the change on the target branch
criteria.contract: POST …/changes answers 201; POST …/changes/<number>/land answers 200 with status landed; GET …/scm/file for each committed path on the target branch answers the committed content

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/scm_test.go, TestSCM_OpenAndLandAChangeWithoutAClone: post(…/scm/commits, {branch:'w', base_ref:'main', operations:[create n/1.txt 'one', create n/2.txt 'two']}); c = post(…/changes, {source:{branch:'w'}, title:'t'}); assert c.status == 201; l = post(…/changes/c.number/land); assert l.status == 200 and l.json.status == 'landed'; assert get(…/scm/file?path=n/1.txt&ref=main, raw).body == 'one' and same for n/2.txt 'two'; the test ran no git command against the hub

criteria.action: for any sequence of file operations committed and landed through the source control API, leave the target branch with the same tree as the equivalent git commits pushed and landed
criteria.contract: the tree id of the target branch head after the API journey equals the tree id of the head of a local repository in which the same file operations were committed with stock git on the same base; a fresh git clone of the workspace passes git fsck

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
the API journey of the previous scenario has run on demo; a local clone of the origin at the same base commit
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/scm_test.go, TestSCM_ResultEqualsEquivalentGitOperations: in the local clone: write n/1.txt 'one' and n/2.txt 'two'; git add; git commit; want = git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}; fresh = git clone <demo remote>; assert git -C fresh rev-parse origin/main^{tree} == want; assert git -C fresh fsck --strict == 0; assert git -C fresh log --format=%P -1 origin/main has one parent

criteria.condition: stock git clones a workspace in full, with --depth 1 and with --filter=blob:none, then fetches and pushes, authenticating with a PAT in the remote URL and through parley credential-helper
criteria.action: serve every one of those operations
criteria.contract: each git command exits 0; the full clone holds every commit of the default branch; the shallow clone holds exactly one commit; the partial clone holds no blob until a checkout asks for it; a commit pushed from each clone is at the head of its branch on the hub

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
alice's PAT with git:read and git:write; git run with an empty HOME, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/git_compat_test.go, TestGit_CloneFetchPushWithPATAndCredentialHelper: a table over auth {PAT in the URL, credential.helper set to '<parley binary> credential-helper' with PARLEY_ENDPOINT_URL and PARLEY_API_KEY in the environment} x clone {full, --depth 1, --filter=blob:none}: code = git clone …; assert code == 0; full: assert git rev-list --count HEAD == number of seeded commits; shallow: assert count == 1; partial: assert git rev-list --objects --missing=print HEAD lists missing blobs before checkout of a second branch; then another clone pushes a commit to side; assert git fetch origin == 0 and origin/side == that commit; commit on a branch named for the row; assert git push origin <branch> == 0 and get(…/scm/refs/heads/<branch>).sha == HEAD

criteria.condition: a caller without read access to a workspace asks for it, over the REST API or over git
criteria.action: answer exactly as for a workspace that does not exist
criteria.contract: over the API, HTTP 404 with error_type not_found and a body equal to the one for an unknown slug; over git, the same status and the same headers and body as for an unknown repository path, so git clone prints the same message for both; nothing in either answer differs but the request id

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
user mallory, signed in, with no organization in common with alice and no access to demo
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/git_compat_test.go, TestGit_UnreadableWorkspaceLooksNonexistent: with mallory's API key, a table over API paths {…/workspaces/X, …/workspaces/X/changes, …/workspaces/X/scm/refs, …/workspaces/X/activity?paths=a} for X in {demo, no-such}: a = get(path with demo); b = get(path with no-such); assert a.status == 404 and b.status == 404; assert a.error.error_type == b.error.error_type == 'not_found'; assert a.error.message == b.error.message; over git: ra = GET /git/<org>/demo.git/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack with mallory's PAT as Basic password; rb = same for no-such.git; assert ra.status == rb.status and ra.body == rb.body and ra.header['WWW-Authenticate'] == rb.header['WWW-Authenticate']; assert stderr of git clone demo with repository names replaced == stderr of git clone no-such

requirements.title: Landing and conflicts
requirements.rationale: Landing without a queue is the product's central claim (criteria 5 and 6): concurrent lands must all succeed when they do not collide, exactly one must win when they do, and a crash must never leave a half-landed change.

criteria.condition: twenty clients each send one land request at the same moment for twenty ready changes that add twenty different files to one target branch
criteria.action: land all twenty on a linear history without any caller having to retry
criteria.contract: each of the twenty first requests is answered HTTP 200 with status landed; the target's history from its previous head has exactly twenty new commits, none with two parents; each change's file is added by exactly one of them; every change has state landed

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main

requirements.rationale: A protected branch is the product's safety line (criteria 9 and 10): it must move only in the three recorded ways, for the same callers on every surface, and what landed must be undoable in one call.

criteria.action: move the protected branch to the landed or fetched commit

requirements.title: Events and webhooks
requirements.rationale: Everything that reacts to the hub reads its events (criterion 12): a consumer that loses one, sees them out of order or cannot trust a delivery cannot be built on.

criteria.contract: the first fifty event frames after the reconnect are the fifty missed events, in strictly ascending seq, none repeated and none before the resume position; an event written after the reconnect arrives next on the same connection

requirements.title: Conventions, operations and carried features
requirements.rationale: A client is written once against the conventions, and an operator runs and backs up one process (criteria 16 and 17); the carried features must be reachable end to end in the same hub (criterion 15).

criteria.action: for any route under /api/v1, answer a request that fails with the error envelope, and a request with a method the path does not have with 405
criteria.contract: for every row of the suite's route table (the route table generated from the PRD's route index, docs/prd/appendix_a_routes.md): a request with no credential is answered 401 with Content-Type application/json; charset=utf-8 and a body {error: {code, message, error_type}} where code equals the status and error_type is unauthenticated (of the two public routes, POST /auth/callback with a malformed body is answered 400 invalid_request in the same shape and GET /auth/providers has no failing request of this kind); a request with a credential and a method no route has for that path is answered 405 with error_type method_not_allowed in the same shape; an unknown path is 404 not_found in the same shape

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
the route table in the suite: method, path with placeholders, and whether the route is public; placeholders are filled with identifiers that exist on the hub
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/conventions_test.go, TestConventions_EveryErrorIsTheEnvelopeAndWrongMethodIs405: assert the (method, path) pairs of routes equal the routes parsed from docs/prd/appendix_a_routes.md; for each row under /api/v1: r = do(row.method, row.path, no Authorization); if row is POST /auth/callback: assertEnvelope(do(POST, row.path, body '{'), 400, 'invalid_request') else if not row.public: assertEnvelope(r, 401, 'unauthenticated'); m = a method in {GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE} that no row has for row.path; if m exists: assertEnvelope(do(m, row.path, admin token), 405, 'method_not_allowed'); assertEnvelope(get('/api/v1/no/such/path', admin token), 404, 'not_found'); assertEnvelope checks status, Content-Type == 'application/json; charset=utf-8', error.code == status, error.error_type == want and error.message is a non-empty string

criteria.action: for any list route, page the result the same way
criteria.contract: for every list route of the suite's route table, with three items present: the answer is {items: array, next_cursor}; with limit=1, following next_cursor three times returns each of the three items exactly once and the last page has next_cursor null; limit=0 and limit=201 answer 400 invalid_request; a cursor taken from another list route answers 400 invalid_request; an empty list answers items [] and next_cursor null

setup: a hub started by the harness from the built parleyd binary; user alice signed in through the fake identity provider; workspace demo registered from a seeded test origin, owned by alice, default branch main
for each list route marked in the route table, a seeding function in the suite that creates three items of that kind through the API
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/conventions_test.go, TestConventions_EveryListPagesTheSameWay: for each list row: empty = get(path on a fresh parent); assert empty.items == [] and empty.next_cursor == null; seed 3; all = get(path).items; assert len(all) >= 3; seen = []; cur = ''; loop: p = get(path + '?limit=1' + cursor); assert len(p.items) == 1; seen += id(p.items[0]); cur = p.next_cursor; until cur == null; assert seen == [id(x) for x in all]; assert no duplicate in seen; for bad in ['0','201']: r = get(path + '?limit=' + bad); assert r.status == 400 and r.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'; r = get(path + '?cursor=' + a cursor of a different list route); assert r.status == 400 and r.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'

criteria.action: for any POST route that creates a resource, honour an Idempotency-Key
criteria.contract: for every creating POST of the suite's route table except POST /auth/callback: a second request with the same key, caller and body answers 200 with the first answer's body, without any member that is shown once (a token or secret value), and the resource exists once; the same key with a different body answers 409 conflict; an empty key and a key of 256 characters answer 400 invalid_request

criteria.action: run from one binary, one configuration file and one data directory
criteria.contract: a parleyd binary copied alone into an empty directory, started with XDG_CONFIG_HOME naming a directory that holds only config.toml, XDG_DATA_HOME naming an empty directory, an empty HOME and a PATH that holds only git, writes its listening line, answers GET /readyz with 200 and serves a workspace creation, a clone, a push and a land; afterwards the binary's directory and HOME hold no new file, the configuration directory holds config.toml and admin_token only, and all other state is under the data directory; no other process was started besides git children that have exited

criteria.contract: parleyd backup exits 0 while eight writers keep getting 2xx answers; a second parleyd started with the snapshot as its data directory writes its listening line and answers GET /readyz with 200; on it, every workspace listed is ready, every change returned by GET …/changes has its version refs fetchable by git, git fsck of a clone passes, a land of an open change answers 200, and its event log's seq values are strictly ascending; parleyd backup into a non-empty directory exits 1

criteria.condition: the suite runs with PARLEY_ACCEPTANCE_REFERENCE_HOST=1 on a host with 8 cores, 32 GB of memory and local SSD storage
criteria.action: meet the latency and throughput targets a single client can observe
criteria.contract: over 100 samples each: fork creation p95 under 1 s; read of one file and of one tree through the API p95 under 100 ms; commit creation of 100 files through the API p95 under 500 ms; land of a change of 20 commits with no contention p95 under 2 s; at least 60 non-conflicting changes landed on one target branch within one minute; an event received by a live subscriber of GET /events within 1 s of the 2xx answer of the request that caused it

setup: a hub started by the harness with default limits; alice; workspace demo from an origin with 1,000 commits and 5,000 files
check.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/performance_test.go, TestPerformance_SingleClientTargetsOfTheReferenceHost: harness.Require(t, ReferenceHost); a table over (operation, samples, bound) {(post forks, 100, p95 < 1 s), (get scm/file, 100, p95 < 100 ms), (get scm/tree, 100, p95 < 100 ms), (post scm/commits with 100 create operations, 100, p95 < 500 ms), (post land of a 20-commit change, 100, p95 < 2 s)}: d = durations; assert percentile(d, 95) < bound; throughput: prepare 80 disjoint ready changes; land them from 8 clients for 60 s; assert landed >= 60; events: 100 x {t0 = time of the 201 of post claims; t1 = arrival at the stream reader}; assert max(t1 - t0) < 1 s

criteria.condition: a developer takes one journey through each carried feature with the parley CLI: a workspace's life, a carry-patch rebuild, a secret and a variable, a forge read, and a session with its audit trail
criteria.action: complete each journey
criteria.contract: every command of the five journeys exits 0, and: the workspace is ready after create --wait, fast_forward after a sync, archived, ready again, and 404 after delete; the carry-patch workspace's integration branch equals upstream's head plus the patch's commit; parley secrets list names the secret and no output of any command holds its value, while parley vars resolve prints the variable's value with its origin; parley issue list prints the two issues the fake forge holds; parley audit query returns the session's events and GET /metrics exposes parley_agent_sessions_active for the workspace

requirements.rationale: An agent runs inside a sandbox the hub controls (criterion 18): the sandbox must arrive with the fork, must never hold a credential the operator did not expose, must be confined on the network, bounded in number, and must survive the hub.

execution_paths.title: An agent forks, pushes and lands

steps.action: runs parley workspace create --name demo --git-url <origin> --wait
sends POST /api/v1/workspaces and polls GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo until its status is ready
clones the origin into the workspace's repository and reports the workspace ready
sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/forks with a token object
creates the fork without copying history, mints the fork-bound token and answers 201 with the fork, its remote and the token
clones the fork's remote with the token, commits a file on a new branch and pushes it with -o parley.change
accepts the push, opens a change on the parent with version 1 and prints its number on the push's remote lines
runs parley change land demo <number> with the fork's token
rebases the change onto the target, moves the default branch by compare-and-swap, marks the change landed and writes parley.change.land
clones the parent and finds the agent's file on the default branch

real_components: the built parleyd binary as its own process with its real stores and repositories on disk
the test origin of internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest served over TLS
the fake identity provider reached through POST /auth/callback
setup: the harness has built both binaries and started a hub on a temporary configuration directory and data directory
alice is signed in through the fake identity provider and holds an API key and a PAT with workspaces:write and tokens:manage
the origin holds three commits on main
end_state: GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo/changes/<number> shows state landed and its one land attempt has status landed
a fresh git clone of demo has the agent's file at the head of main, and main's history is linear
GET /api/v1/events/log?workspace=demo holds parley.workspace.fork, parley.git.push, parley.change.open and parley.change.land in ascending seq
the fork's token still answers 404 on a second workspace
smoke.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/journey_test.go, TestJourney_AgentForksPushesAndLands: hub = harness.Start(t); alice = hub.User('alice'); origin = hub.Origin(3 commits); assert cli(alice,'workspace','create','--name','demo','--git-url',origin.URL,'--wait').json.status == 'ready'; f = post(…/workspaces/demo/forks, {token:{permissions:[git:read, git:write, changes:read, changes:write]}}); git clone f.remote with f.token.token; write agent.txt; commit on branch task; out = git push -o parley.change origin task; n = the one open change of demo; l = cli(f.token.token,'change','land','demo',n); assert l.code == 0 and l.json.status == 'landed'; fresh = git clone demo; assert agent.txt in fresh at origin/main; assert types of get(/events/log?workspace=demo) contain the four types in ascending seq

execution_paths.title: Two agents race to land and the loser resolves without a clone

steps.action: two agents, each on its own fork, push a change that replaces the same line of the same file
opens both changes and reports each mergeable clean against the target
both send POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/changes/<number>/land at the same moment
lands one change by compare-and-swap; rebasing the other onto the moved target conflicts, so it ends that attempt as conflict and answers 409 land_conflict with the conflict report
the losing agent reads GET …/changes/<number>/conflict/file?path=<file> and runs parley change resolve with the resolved content
sends POST …/changes/<number>/restack with the resolution
rebuilds the change's commits on the target with the resolved file, moves the source branch and records a new version
the losing agent sends the land request again
lands the change and writes parley.change.land

real_components: the built parleyd binary as its own process
the hub's real git rebase and compare-and-swap of refs
setup: a hub with workspace demo whose src/a.txt has five lines
two forks of demo, each with a bound token
end_state: src/a.txt on main holds the resolved content the losing agent submitted and no conflict marker
GET …/lands lists three attempts: landed, conflict, landed
the event log holds parley.change.land_fail for the loser's first attempt and parley.change.land for both changes
smoke.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/journey_test.go, TestJourney_TwoAgentsRaceAndTheLoserResolves: open p (fork 1) and q (fork 2) editing line 3 of src/a.txt; rp, rq = concurrent post(…/land) with each fork's token; assert sorted([rp.status, rq.status]) == [200, 409]; loser = the 409 one; assert loser.error.error_type == 'land_conflict'; body = get(…/changes/<loser>/conflict/file?path=src/a.txt).body; assert '<<<<<<<' in body; cli(loser token,'change','resolve','demo',loser,'--file','src/a.txt=<resolved>'); assert cli(loser token,'change','land','demo',loser).json.status == 'landed'; assert get(…/scm/file?path=src/a.txt&ref=main, raw).body == resolved; assert [a.status for a in get(…/lands).items oldest first] == ['landed','conflict','landed']

execution_paths.title: A consumer resumes the event stream

steps.action: opens GET /api/v1/events?workspace=demo with a PAT holding audit:read and reads events as they are written
sends a heartbeat and then each visible event of the workspace as an SSE frame whose id is the event's seq
disconnects, remembering the last seq it received
pushes, opens a change and lands it while the consumer is away
writes each event to the event log with the next seq, in the same transaction as the state change it reports
reconnects with Last-Event-ID set to the remembered seq
replays every event after that seq in ascending order, then continues with live events on the same connection
reports a check on the change it learned of from the replayed parley.change.open event

real_components: the built parleyd binary as its own process
the event log in the hub's store
the SSE stream of GET /api/v1/events over a real TCP connection
the built parley binary for parley events tail
setup: a hub with workspace demo
user ci with write access to demo and a PAT holding audit:read, changes:read and checks:write
end_state: the events received after the reconnect equal GET /api/v1/events/log?workspace=demo&after=<remembered seq>, in the same order, followed by one live event
no seq was received twice and none at or below the remembered seq
GET …/changes/<number>/checks lists the check the review agent reported
smoke.pseudocode: in test/acceptance/journey_test.go, TestJourney_ConsumerResumesTheEventStream: r = stream(/events?workspace=demo, ci PAT); create a claim; s0 = r.Next(1).seq; r.Close(); push a branch with -o parley.change; land it; open a second change n2; want = get(/events/log?workspace=demo&after=s0).items; r2 = stream(/events?workspace=demo, Last-Event-ID: s0); got = r2.Next(len(want)); assert [e.seq for e in got] == [e.seq for e in want]; create a claim; assert r2.Next(1).seq > got[-1].seq; n = number from the parley.change.open event of n2 in got; put(…/changes/n/checks/test, {status:'passed'}, ci PAT); assert get(…/changes/n/checks).items[0].name == 'test'
